chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who wears a bed-cover, the back of which is red and its lining is yellow, which has been worn for a year and two years. He (peace be upon him) said: 'As long as it does not have a smell, there is no problem; and every garment that is dyed and washed, it is permissible to wear Ihram in it. But if it is not washed, then no.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a garment to be valid for Ihram if it is old or dyed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the validity of Ihram clothing depends on ritual purity rather than aesthetic features like color or age, provided the garment is free from impurity (indicated by a distinct smell) and has been washed. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that Ihram garments need not be white or new, but must be clean and free from *najis* elements, reflecting the practical flexibility granted to pilgrims in their attire.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaw Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Bin Musa who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who wears the bed-cover, the back of which is reddish and its inside is yellowish, a year and two years having passed for it. Heasws said: ‘As long as there does not happen to be a smell for it, so there is no problem; and every cloth dyed and washed, it is allowed to wear Ihraam in it. But if it is not washed, so no’.
en.sarwar: 21. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Najih who has said the following:
“Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is not harmful for one in the state of Ihram to wear a ring.’ In another Hadith it is said that it must not be worn for beautification.”
